sections.title: Paper 1
sections.instructions: Answer all questions. You are not allowed to use a calculator.

items.stem:
Complete the fraction calculation. Write your answer as a fraction.

3/8 + 4/8 =
items.note: Mark scheme: 7/8. Printed as the first of two calculations in Question 1 [2]; 1 mark each.

items.stem:
Complete the fraction calculation. Write your answer as a fraction.

4/7 − 3/7 =
items.note: Mark scheme: 1/7. Printed as the second of two calculations in Question 1 [2]; 1 mark each.

items.stem: Write the 4-digit number that is equivalent to 5000 + 300 + 20 + 8

accepted: five thousand three hundred and twenty eight
five thousand three hundred and twenty-eight
five thousand, three hundred and twenty-eight

items.note: Mark scheme: 5328. Accept the number written in words.

items.stem:
Here are some pictures of shapes that fold to make 3D shapes.

Match each shape that folds to the name of the correct 3D shape.
items.note: Mark scheme: all three lines correct for the mark. Also accepts the net of the cube joined to ‘cuboid’.

items.stem: Select all the multiples of 2
items.note: Mark scheme: 202 and 518 and 722. All three for the mark (paper: draw a ring around all the multiples of 2).

items.stem:
Here is part of a sequence.

14, 9, 4, … (each term is 5 less than the one before)

The sequence continues in the same way.

Write the next term in the sequence.
items.note: Mark scheme: –1

items.stem: Match each calculation to the correct answer.
items.note: Mark scheme: all three correct for the mark. Two calculations share the answer 3600 and only two answer labels are printed.

items.stem:
Here is a drawing of a cuboid.

Write the correct number to complete the sentence.

A cuboid has ___ faces.
items.note: Mark scheme: 6

items.stem:
Oliver cuts one whole strip of paper into five equal pieces.

Oliver says, ‘Each piece is 1/6 of the whole.’

Is Oliver correct? Answer Yes or No, and explain how you know.

accepted: No, there are five pieces so each piece is a fifth
No, there are 5 pieces so each is 1/5 not 1/6
No, each piece is one fifth
No, five equal pieces are fifths
No, it is cut into 5 pieces so each is one fifth
No, there are only 5 shapes so each is a fifth not a sixth

items.note: Mark scheme: ticks ‘No’ AND an explanation recognising that the pieces are fifths (e.g. there are only 5 shapes so each is a fifth not a sixth). Accept any reasonable explanation. A person should check this answer against the mark scheme.

items.stem: Write the number of seconds in 5 minutes.
items.note: Mark scheme: 300 (seconds)

items.stem:
Here are some numbers in a Carroll diagram.

The top row contains 10, 100 (left column) and 25, 175 (right column). The bottom row contains 4, 12 (left column) and 7, 29 (right column).

Complete the labels to make the Carroll diagram correct.

Write the label for the COLUMNS (the left column is ‘……’ and the right column is ‘Not ……’).
items.note: Mark scheme: labels completed to indicate multiples of 2 (columns) and multiples of 5 (rows); 1 mark per correct pair of headings. Accept any valid labels, e.g. ‘in the 2 times table’ / ‘even numbers’. Printed as Question 11 [2]. A person should check this answer against the mark scheme.

items.stem:
Same Carroll diagram as before.

Write the label for the ROWS (the top row is ‘……’ and the bottom row is ‘Not ……’).
items.note: Mark scheme: multiples of 5 for the row headings; 1 mark per correct pair of headings. Accept any valid labels. Printed as Question 11 [2]. A person should check this answer against the mark scheme.

items.stem:
Here are some mathematical symbols: <, >, =

Choose the symbols that make both statements correct.

42 ÷ 6 ☐ 42 ÷ 7

63 ÷ 9 ☐ 64 ÷ 8
items.note: Mark scheme: > then <; both symbols correct for the mark. Paper asks the learner to write a symbol in each box; presented as a choice.

items.stem: Write three thousand one hundred and nine in figures.
items.note: Mark scheme: 3109

items.stem:
Here are some shapes drawn on triangular dotty paper.

Match each shape to the correct description.
items.note: Mark scheme: all three lines correct for the mark. Two shapes match ‘regular polygon’.

items.stem:
Here are the first three terms in a sequence.

102, 50, 24

The term-to-term rule is, ‘Subtract 2 from the previous term and then divide the answer by 2’

Write the 4th term in the sequence.
items.note: Mark scheme: 11
Mark scheme: 643

items.stem:
Complete each sentence.

The value of the digit 1 in 615 is ……

The value of the digit 1 in 5 215 632 is ……

Write both values in order, separated by a comma.
items.note: Mark scheme: ten and ten thousand; both correct for the mark. Accept 10 and 10 000.

items.stem:
The children in Class 4 count the vehicles passing their school.

They count the vehicles between 07:30 and 08:30
They also count the vehicles between 11:00 and 12:00

The bar charts show their results.

Write how many more buses pass their school between 07:30 and 08:30 than between 11:00 and 12:00
items.note: Mark scheme: 16. Accept answers in the range 14–18 inclusive.

items.stem:
Look at the same bar charts.

Suggest a reason why there were more cars passing their school between 07:30 and 08:30 than between 11:00 and 12:00

accepted: more people were driving to work
more people were going to school
people were taking children to school
people go to work in the morning
parents were driving children to school

items.note: Mark scheme: a reasonable explanation, e.g. more people were driving to work / more people were going to school. Accept any reasonable explanation. A person should check this answer against the mark scheme.

items.stem:
Here is part of a train timetable.

Peterborough 10:10, 10:35, 11:10
Doncaster 11:25, 11:50, 12:25
Leeds 12:05, 12:35, 13:05
Edinburgh 15:45, 16:15, 16:45

Mia lives in Doncaster.
She travels on the train to Edinburgh.
She arrives before 4.00 pm.

Write the time of Mia’s train from Doncaster.
items.note: Mark scheme: 11:25. Accept equivalent times such as twenty five minutes past eleven.

items.stem:
Here is a dot plot.

The dot plot shows the scores from a spelling test.

Work out the number of children who scored 5 or lower in the test.
items.note: Mark scheme: 8

items.stem:
Look at the same dot plot.

Write the correct number to complete the sentence.

The same number of children scored 0 and ___ in the test.
items.note: Mark scheme: 7

items.stem:
A shop sells notepads and pencils.

Notepad: 3 dollars and 80 cents
Pencil A: 1 dollar and 50 cents
Pencil B: 1 dollar and 80 cents
Pencil C: 2 dollars

Hassan buys one notepad and three pencils.
He pays with a 10 dollar note and gets 1 dollar and 40 cents change.

Work out the items Hassan buys. He buys 1 notepad. Write how many of each pencil he buys in the form ‘Pencil A: …, Pencil B: …, Pencil C: …’. Show your working.

accepted: Pencil A: 2, Pencil B: 1, Pencil C: 0
Pencil A 2, Pencil B 1, Pencil C 0
2 of Pencil A and 1 of Pencil B
two of pencil A and one of pencil B

items.note: Mark scheme: Pencil A 2, Pencil B 1, Pencil C 0 (Pencil C may be left blank) for 2 marks. Award 1 mark for 10 dollars – (3 dollars 80 cents + 1 dollar 40 cents) whether or not evaluated correctly, or for 4 dollars 80 cents seen. A person should check the working for the part mark.

items.stem:
Lily has a party.

She invites 45 friends.
She gives each friend a balloon.
Balloons are sold in packs of 8

Work out the smallest number of packs of balloons Lily buys.
items.note: Mark scheme: 6 (packs of balloons). Do not accept 5 remainder 5.

omitted.why: draw four equilateral triangles arranged to make a larger triangle on dotty paper [2]
shade 1/5 of a shape made from 20 squares (any 4 squares) [1]
draw the reflection of a shape in a mirror line on a grid [1]
